raw_graphql_pull_request.body: ## Motivation [Foundry](https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry) persists CUDA graphs across restarts. The first start (`save`) archives the captured graphs, their kernels and the device-memory layout. Later starts (`load`) rebuild the graphs from the archive instead of capturing them, so an engine that spends 40-120 s capturing 128 decode graphs per rank is serving within a few seconds of the eager engine. Foundry hooks the CUDA driver (an `LD_PRELOAD` library, like `torch_memory_saver`) and needs SGLang to call it at a few points of the engine bring-up. This PR adds it the way SGLang integrates `torch_memory_saver`: an optional dependency behind an adapter that is a no-op unless the feature is enabled, a server argument, and explicit one-line call sites. The call sites pass only the values Foundry needs (the loaded model, the draft-worker flag, the resolved pool config, the prefill request slots), never a runner or backend object. It replaces the plugin approach of #41791, which maintainers considered unsuitable for an extension that needs runtime call sites. **No-op guarantee:** with `--cuda-graph-persistence` unset, every call site resolves to the no-op adapter and no runtime path changes. ## Modifications Four commits on `main` (`[Feature]`, `[Test]`, `[CI]`, `[Docs]`), 25 files, +1327 / -1. `layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py` and the other runner backends are not touched. - **Server arguments**: `--cuda-graph-persistence {save,load}` (default off) and `--cuda-graph-persistence-config PATH` (Foundry TOML; the flag's mode wins over the file's). - **Adapter** (`srt/utils/foundry_adapter.py`, the `torch_memory_saver_adapter.py` shape): lazy import of `foundry.integration.sglang.api`; `create(enable)` returns the real or the no-op adapter, raises with an install hint only when the flag is set and Foundry is missing, and checks `INTEGRATION_API_VERSION` 2.x. Optional extra `sglang[foundry] = ["foundry-core>=0.1.0rc2,<0.2"]`. - **Resolution** (`arg_groups/cuda_graph_hook.py`): pins the fields a restored graph cannot replay and rejects unsupported features (speculative decoding, LoRA, non-full graph backends, ...); every pin states its reason. - **Call sites** (Foundry integration API 2.0). Each is one adapter call or one `with` and passes plain values, never a runner or backend: | site | call | |---|---| | `engine.py`, `data_parallel_controller.py` (the two scheduler spawn sites, next to `memory_saver_adapter.configure_subprocess`) | `configure_subprocess(server_args)`: hook preload scoped to the spawn | | `run_scheduler_process`, `run_data_parallel_controller_process` (before `publish`) | `activate_foundry(server_args)` | | `bootstrap.init_parallel_runtime` | `before_parallel_init(device)` / `after_parallel_init()` | | `ModelRunner.init_torch_distributed` (end) | `after_runner_distributed_init(is_draft_worker)` | | `KVCacheConfigurator._resolve_memory_pool_config` | `replay_saved_memory_pool_config()` / `record_memory_pool_overrides()`: `load` reuses the pool config `save` resolved, because the pool sizes come from a free-memory profile that differs between the two | | `ModelRunner.alloc_memory_pool` (begin / end) | `before_alloc_memory_pool(is_draft_worker)` / `after_alloc_memory_pool(memory_pool_config=..., is_draft_worker=...)` | | `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture`, `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture` | `with capture_scope(phase, model=..., req_slots=None)`; the existing body moves unchanged into `_capture_graphs()` and SGLang's own capture loop still runs | | `FullCudaGraphBackend.capture_one` | `capture_one(shape_key, forward_fn, pool=..., stream=...)`: `save` captures and archives, `load` restores in place of capturing; the backend stores the returned graph and output | | `_set_envs_and_config` | `apply_env_pins(server_args)` | Foundry pins `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1` in the scheduler processes because `save` runs each shape's first forward inside the capture and torch >= 2.14 refuses to trace during capture; SGLang's remaining `@torch.compile` helpers then run eagerly. - **Tests**: `test/registered/unit/utils/test_foundry_adapter.py` (CPU: the adapter against a stub API, plus an AST contract on every call site and its exact arguments); `test/registered/cuda_graph/persistence/test_cuda_graph_persistence.py` and `test_cuda_graph_persistence_prefill.py` (1 GPU, nightly: native, `save`, `load` on Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3-1.7B with prefill graphs; greedy parity, TPOT, restore time, no hook errors). - **CI**: `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_foundry.sh` installs the extra with `--no-deps` from the wheel index of the installed torch/CUDA pair; suite `nightly-test-1-gpu-large-foundry` on runner `1-gpu-large-foundry` (the `1-gpu-h100` pool) in `nightly-test-nvidia.yml`. The runners need PyPI access and the two models in the HF cache. - **Docs**: `advanced_features/cuda_graph_persistence.mdx` (registered in `docs.json`) and two rows in `server_arguments.mdx`. ## Accuracy Tests This PR changes no model outputs and no kernels. The restored graphs are checked with a strict comparison of the native graph, `save` and `load` engines on the same host, code and weights: 74 requests (9 batched calls of 1-32 requests, greedy, 12 tokens), comparing the selected token and the top-3 logprobs of every step, batched and one request at a time. A layout passes when every pair (native/save, native/load, save/load) has identical tokens and a logprob max-abs difference of 0. Per-layout results are in the "strict check" column below. - **E2E tests** on H200: 12/12 passed (6 per file). Greedy output of `save` and `load` is token-identical to native, restore takes 0.02-0.15 s (8 graphs), and median `load` TPOT is 4.50 vs 4.41 ms native (Qwen3.5-2B) and 3.61 vs 3.61 ms (Qwen3-1.7B). - **CPU**: adapter and call-site tests pass (12 tests, 33 subtests). Deleting any call site, or passing a runner where a value is expected, fails the contract test. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The PR does not touch the inference path; the numbers measure Foundry's startup effect through these call sites. Setup: - 4xH200, this branch + foundry-core 0.1.0rc2, torch 2.14.1 / cu130, overlap scheduler on. - Decode graphs for batch sizes 1-128 (1-256 on three rows). Prefill FULL graphs at power-of-two buckets where SGLang can capture them (Qwen3 family, gpt-oss). Qwen3.5, DeepSeek-V4 and GLM run decode graphs only, an SGLang limitation. - TTFT: 128 prompts of the largest bucket at concurrency 32, after a throwaway pass. TPOT: decode bench. *Seconds from launch to the first `/health` 200 in the engine log, rank-0 stages. Load bars show restore only (Foundry's `Loaded N graphs`).* *Text = load / native − 1. "(decode graphs only)": SGLang cannot capture FULL prefill graphs for that model, so its TTFT is the eager prefill on both engines. Faded TPOT bars: bs 1 is below the attention-TP multiple and runs eagerly on both engines.* | model / layout | weights | graphs per rank (prefill + decode) | native /health -> LOAD /health (s) | restore (s, decode + prefill) | strict check (seq / batched) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 EP4 | real | 10 + 128 | 77.5 -> 39.2 | 0.71 + 0.05 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 | real | 12 + 128 | 74.8 -> 36.8 | 0.54 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 attn TP2 x DP2 + EP4 | real | 10 + 128 | 89.7 -> 39.5 | 0.78 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 EP2 | real | 10 + 128 | 72.9 -> 36.7 | 0.73 + 0.05 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 attn TP4 + EP4 | real | 10 + 128 | 81.2 -> 47.1 | 0.73 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 DP4 | real | 12 + 128 | 103.3 -> 46.2 | 0.58 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 + EP2 | real | 10 + 128 | 76.8 -> 35.9 | 0.75 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B EP4 | dummy | 0 + 256 | 100.1 -> 34.8 | 1.28 | exact / tokens exact, logprob 0.002 ¹ | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B attn TP4 + EP4 | dummy | 0 + 128 | 76.5 -> 35.8 | 0.90 | exact / exact | | Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 EP4 | dummy | 0 + 128 | 114.0 -> 42.2 | 0.97 | exact / exact | | Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 attn TP2 x DP2 + EP4 | dummy | 0 + 256 | 180.4 -> 38.3 | 3.62 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 attn TP4 + EP4 | dummy | 10 + 128 | 134.3 -> 35.6 | 1.56 + 0.13 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 attn TP2 x DP2 + EP4 | dummy | 10 + 128 | 143.7 -> 35.2 | 1.60 + 0.13 | exact / exact | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 EP4 | dummy | 0 + 256 | 167.9 -> 39.6 | 2.75 | exact / exact | | GLM-5.3-Flash EP4 | dummy | 0 + 128 | 135.4 -> 51.0 | 1.04 | exact / exact | | gpt-oss-120b EP4 | dummy | 10 + 128 | 87.7 -> 42.3 | 0.63 + 0.05 | see below | | 1-GPU e2e (Qwen3.5-2B; Qwen3-1.7B + prefill) | real | 8 | 12/12 tests passed | 0.02-0.15 | greedy parity | Each `/health` time is the first `200` after launch in the engine log, one run per row. The gpt-oss output is not comparable (dummy mxfp4 experts); graph == load parity holds and save/load sequential is exact. +"""Adapter for Foundry CUDA graph persistence (``--cuda-graph-persistence``).
+
+Foundry (https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry, optional dependency
+``sglang[foundry]``) saves the captured CUDA graphs and the memory layout they
+reference on a first start (``save``) and rebuilds them from that archive on
+later starts (``load``) instead of capturing. It runs a CUDA driver hook in
+the scheduler processes (``LD_PRELOAD``, set by ``configure_subprocess()``
+around their spawn) and is called from the call sites below; the methods of
+the no-op adapter do nothing, so the call sites stay unconditional.
+
+Call sites: the resolution steps in ``arg_groups/cuda_graph_hook.py``,
+``_set_envs_and_config`` and the scheduler spawns (``entrypoints/engine.py``,
+``managers/data_parallel_controller.py``), ``run_scheduler_process``,
+``bootstrap.init_parallel_runtime``, ``ModelRunner.init_torch_distributed`` and
+``alloc_memory_pool``, ``KVCacheConfigurator._resolve_memory_pool_config``, the
+decode / prefill runners' ``capture``, ``FullCudaGraphBackend.capture_one`` and
+``DecodeCudaGraphRunner._resolve_shared_read_ends``.
+
+Foundry is imported only when the flag is set: importing it loads its CUDA
+extension, which a server without the flag must not pay for.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from typing import Any, Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Major version of foundry.integration.sglang.api this adapter calls.
+FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MAJOR = 1
+# Distribution name and minimum version, checked when the flag is set.
+FOUNDRY_PACKAGE = "foundry"
+FOUNDRY_MIN_VERSION = "0.0.3"
+FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT = (
+    'Install it with `pip install --no-build-isolation "sglang[foundry]"` (its CUDA '
+    "extension is built against the installed torch; see "
+    "docs/advanced_features/cuda_graph_persistence)."
+)
+
+
+class FoundryAdapter:
+    """No-op base: what every process uses unless ``--cuda-graph-persistence``
+    is set."""
+
+    enabled = False
+    mode: Optional[str] = None
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def create(
+        enable: bool, mode: Optional[str] = None, config_path: Optional[str] = None
+    ) -> "FoundryAdapter":
+        if not enable:
+            return FoundryAdapter()
+        return _FoundryAdapterReal(_import_foundry_api(), mode, config_path)
+
+    # Resolution (launcher).
+    def pin_server_args(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def validate_graph_config(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def validate_resolved_server_args(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def apply_env_pins(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    # Process spawn.
+    @contextmanager
+    def configure_subprocess(self, server_args: Any = None):
+        yield
+
+    # Scheduler process.
+    def before_parallel_init(self, device: str) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def after_parallel_init(self) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def after_runner_distributed_init(self, model_runner: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def replay_saved_memory_pool_config(self):
+        return None
+
+    def record_memory_pool_overrides(self) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def before_alloc_memory_pool(self, model_runner: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def after_alloc_memory_pool(self, model_runner: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def capture_scope(self, runner: Any):
+        yield
+
+    def capture_one(self, backend: Any, shape_key: Any, forward_fn) -> None:
+        raise RuntimeError("capture_one is only called when Foundry is enabled")
+
+    def shared_read_ends_override(self, runner, attn_backend, forward_mode):
+        return None
+
+
+class _FoundryAdapterReal(FoundryAdapter):
+    enabled = True
+
+    def __init__(self, api, mode: str, config_path: Optional[str]):
+        self._api = api
+        self.mode = mode
+        api.activate(mode=mode, config_path=config_path)
+
+    def pin_server_args(self, server_args):
+        self._api.pin_server_args(server_args)
+
+    def validate_graph_config(self, server_args):
+        self._api.validate_graph_config(server_args)
+
+    def validate_resolved_server_args(self, server_args):
+        self._api.validate_resolved_server_args(server_args)
+
+    def apply_env_pins(self, server_args):
+        self._api.apply_env_pins(server_args)
+
+    def configure_subprocess(self, server_args=None):
+        return self._api.configure_subprocess(server_args)
+
+    def before_parallel_init(self, device):
+        self._api.before_parallel_init(device)
+
+    def after_parallel_init(self):
+        self._api.after_parallel_init()
+
+    def after_runner_distributed_init(self, model_runner):
+        self._api.after_runner_distributed_init(model_runner)
+
+    def replay_saved_memory_pool_config(self):
+        return self._api.replay_saved_memory_pool_config()
+
+    def record_memory_pool_overrides(self):
+        self._api.record_memory_pool_overrides()
+
+    def before_alloc_memory_pool(self, model_runner):
+        self._api.before_alloc_memory_pool(model_runner)
+
+    def after_alloc_memory_pool(self, model_runner):
+        self._api.after_alloc_memory_pool(model_runner)
+
+    def capture_scope(self, runner):
+        return self._api.capture_scope(runner)
+
+    def capture_one(self, backend, shape_key, forward_fn):
+        self._api.capture_one(backend, shape_key, forward_fn)
+
+    def shared_read_ends_override(self, runner, attn_backend, forward_mode):
+        return self._api.shared_read_ends_override(runner, attn_backend, forward_mode)
+
+
+def _import_foundry_api():
+    try:
+        from foundry.integration.sglang import api
+    except ImportError as e:
+        logger.warning(
+            "--cuda-graph-persistence is set, but Foundry is not installed. %s",
+            FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT,
+        )
+        raise e
+    from sglang.srt.utils.common import assert_pkg_version
+
+    assert_pkg_version(FOUNDRY_PACKAGE, FOUNDRY_MIN_VERSION, FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT)
+    found = getattr(api, "INTEGRATION_API_VERSION", None)
+    if found is None or found[0] != FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MAJOR:
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Foundry integration API {found} is not supported by this SGLang, which "
+            f"needs major version {FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MAJOR}. {FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT}"
+        )
+    return api
+
+
+_NOOP = FoundryAdapter()
+_active: FoundryAdapter = _NOOP
+
+
+def get_foundry_adapter() -> FoundryAdapter:
+    """This process's adapter: the one ``activate_foundry`` created, else the
+    no-op one."""
+    return _active
+
+
+def activate_foundry(server_args: Any) -> FoundryAdapter:
+    """Create this process's adapter from the raw ``--cuda-graph-persistence``
+    and ``--cuda-graph-persistence-config`` of ``server_args``. Idempotent;
+    run by the first resolution step in the launcher and at the top of the
+    scheduler and data-parallel-controller processes."""
+    global _active
+    mode = getattr(server_args, "cuda_graph_persistence", None)

The first start (`save`) archives the captured graphs, their kernels and the device-memory layout. Later starts (`load`) rebuild the graphs from the archive instead of capturing them, so an engine that spends 40-120 s capturing 128 decode graphs per rank is serving within a few seconds of the eager engine. Foundry hooks the CUDA driver (an `LD_PRELOAD` library, like `torch_memory_saver`) and needs SGLang to call it at a few points of the engine bring-up. This PR adds it the way SGLang integrates `torch_memory_saver`: an optional dependency behind an adapter that is a no-op unless the feature is enabled, a server argument, and explicit one-line call sites. The call sites pass only the values Foundry needs (the loaded model, the draft-worker flag, the resolved pool config, the prefill request slots), never a runner or backend object. It replaces the plugin approach of #41791, which maintainers considered unsuitable for an extension that needs runtime call sites. **No-op guarantee:** with `--cuda-graph-persistence` unset, every call site resolves to the no-op adapter and no runtime path changes. ## Modifications Four commits on `main` (`[Feature]`, `[Test]`, `[CI]`, `[Docs]`), 25 files, +1327 / -1. `layers/moe/token_dispatcher/standard.py` and the other runner backends are not touched. - **Server arguments**: `--cuda-graph-persistence {save,load}` (default off) and `--cuda-graph-persistence-config PATH` (Foundry TOML; the flag's mode wins over the file's). - **Adapter** (`srt/utils/foundry_adapter.py`, the `torch_memory_saver_adapter.py` shape): lazy import of `foundry.integration.sglang.api`; `create(enable)` returns the real or the no-op adapter, raises with an install hint only when the flag is set and Foundry is missing, and checks `INTEGRATION_API_VERSION` 2.x. Optional extra `sglang[foundry] = ["foundry-core>=0.1.0rc2,<0.2"]`. - **Resolution** (`arg_groups/cuda_graph_hook.py`): pins the fields a restored graph cannot replay and rejects unsupported features (speculative decoding, LoRA, non-full graph backends, ...); every pin states its reason. - **Call sites** (Foundry integration API 2.0). Each is one adapter call or one `with` and passes plain values, never a runner or backend: | site | call | |---|---| | `engine.py`, `data_parallel_controller.py` (the two scheduler spawn sites, next to `memory_saver_adapter.configure_subprocess`) | `configure_subprocess(server_args)`: hook preload scoped to the spawn | | `run_scheduler_process`, `run_data_parallel_controller_process` (before `publish`) | `activate_foundry(server_args)` | | `bootstrap.init_parallel_runtime` | `before_parallel_init(device)` / `after_parallel_init()` | | `ModelRunner.init_torch_distributed` (end) | `after_runner_distributed_init(is_draft_worker)` | | `KVCacheConfigurator._resolve_memory_pool_config` | `replay_saved_memory_pool_config()` / `record_memory_pool_overrides()`: `load` reuses the pool config `save` resolved, because the pool sizes come from a free-memory profile that differs between the two | | `ModelRunner.alloc_memory_pool` (begin / end) | `before_alloc_memory_pool(is_draft_worker)` / `after_alloc_memory_pool(memory_pool_config=..., is_draft_worker=...)` | | `DecodeCudaGraphRunner.capture`, `PrefillCudaGraphRunner.capture` | `with capture_scope(phase, model=..., req_slots=None)`; the existing body moves unchanged into `_capture_graphs()` and SGLang's own capture loop still runs | | `FullCudaGraphBackend.capture_one` | `capture_one(shape_key, forward_fn, pool=..., stream=...)`: `save` captures and archives, `load` restores in place of capturing; the backend stores the returned graph and output | | `_set_envs_and_config` | `apply_env_pins(server_args)` | Foundry pins `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1` in the scheduler processes because `save` runs each shape's first forward inside the capture and torch >= 2.14 refuses to trace during capture; SGLang's remaining `@torch.compile` helpers then run eagerly. - **Tests**: `test/registered/unit/utils/test_foundry_adapter.py` (CPU: the adapter against a stub API, plus an AST contract on every call site and its exact arguments); `test/registered/cuda_graph/persistence/test_cuda_graph_persistence.py` and `test_cuda_graph_persistence_prefill.py` (1 GPU, nightly: native, `save`, `load` on Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3-1.7B with prefill graphs; greedy parity, TPOT, restore time, no hook errors). - **CI**: `scripts/ci/cuda/ci_install_foundry.sh` installs the extra with `--no-deps` from the wheel index of the installed torch/CUDA pair; suite `nightly-test-1-gpu-large-foundry` on runner `1-gpu-large-foundry` (the `1-gpu-h100` pool) in `nightly-test-nvidia.yml`. The runners need PyPI access and the two models in the HF cache. - **Docs**: `advanced_features/cuda_graph_persistence.mdx` (registered in `docs.json`) and two rows in `server_arguments.mdx`. ## Accuracy Tests This PR changes no model outputs and no kernels. The restored graphs are checked with a strict comparison of the native graph, `save` and `load` engines on the same host, code and weights: 74 requests (9 batched calls of 1-32 requests, greedy, 12 tokens), comparing the selected token and the top-3 logprobs of every step, batched and one request at a time. A layout passes when every pair (native/save, native/load, save/load) has identical tokens and a logprob max-abs difference of 0. Per-layout results are in the "strict check" column below. - **E2E tests** on H200: 12/12 passed (6 per file). Greedy output of `save` and `load` is token-identical to native, restore takes 0.02-0.15 s (8 graphs), and median `load` TPOT is 4.50 vs 4.41 ms native (Qwen3.5-2B) and 3.61 vs 3.61 ms (Qwen3-1.7B). - **CPU**: adapter and call-site tests pass (12 tests, 33 subtests). Deleting any call site, or passing a runner where a value is expected, fails the contract test. ## Speed Tests and Profiling The PR does not touch the inference path; the numbers measure Foundry's startup effect through these call sites. Setup: - 4xH200, this branch + foundry-core 0.1.0rc2, torch 2.14.1 / cu130, overlap scheduler on. - Decode graphs for batch sizes 1-128 (1-256 on three rows). Prefill FULL graphs at power-of-two buckets where SGLang can capture them (Qwen3 family, gpt-oss). Qwen3.5, DeepSeek-V4 and GLM run decode graphs only, an SGLang limitation. - TTFT: 128 prompts of the largest bucket at concurrency 32, after a throwaway pass. TPOT: decode bench. *Seconds from launch to the first `/health` 200 in the engine log, rank-0 stages. Load bars show restore only (Foundry's `Loaded N graphs`).* *Text = load / native − 1. "(decode graphs only)": SGLang cannot capture FULL prefill graphs for that model, so its TTFT is the eager prefill on both engines. Faded TPOT bars: bs 1 is below the attention-TP multiple and runs eagerly on both engines.* | model / layout | weights | graphs per rank (prefill + decode) | native /health -> LOAD /health (s) | restore (s, decode + prefill) | strict check (seq / batched) | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 EP4 | real | 10 + 128 | 77.5 -> 39.2 | 0.71 + 0.05 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 | real | 12 + 128 | 74.8 -> 36.8 | 0.54 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 attn TP2 x DP2 + EP4 | real | 10 + 128 | 89.7 -> 39.5 | 0.78 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 EP2 | real | 10 + 128 | 72.9 -> 36.7 | 0.73 + 0.05 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 attn TP4 + EP4 | real | 10 + 128 | 81.2 -> 47.1 | 0.73 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 DP4 | real | 12 + 128 | 103.3 -> 46.2 | 0.58 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 TP2 + EP2 | real | 10 + 128 | 76.8 -> 35.9 | 0.75 + 0.06 | exact / exact | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B EP4 | dummy | 0 + 256 | 100.1 -> 34.8 | 1.28 | exact / tokens exact, logprob 0.002 ¹ | | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B attn TP4 + EP4 | dummy | 0 + 128 | 76.5 -> 35.8 | 0.90 | exact / exact | | Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 EP4 | dummy | 0 + 128 | 114.0 -> 42.2 | 0.97 | exact / exact | | Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 attn TP2 x DP2 + EP4 | dummy | 0 + 256 | 180.4 -> 38.3 | 3.62 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 attn TP4 + EP4 | dummy | 10 + 128 | 134.3 -> 35.6 | 1.56 + 0.13 | exact / exact | | Qwen3-235B-A22B-FP8 attn TP2 x DP2 + EP4 | dummy | 10 + 128 | 143.7 -> 35.2 | 1.60 + 0.13 | exact / exact | | DeepSeek-V4-Flash-FP8 EP4 | dummy | 0 + 256 | 167.9 -> 39.6 | 2.75 | exact / exact | | GLM-5.3-Flash EP4 | dummy | 0 + 128 | 135.4 -> 51.0 | 1.04 | exact / exact | | gpt-oss-120b EP4 | dummy | 10 + 128 | 87.7 -> 42.3 | 0.63 + 0.05 | see below | | 1-GPU e2e (Qwen3.5-2B; Qwen3-1.7B + prefill) | real | 8 | 12/12 tests passed | 0.02-0.15 | greedy parity | Each `/health` time is the first `200` after launch in the engine log, one run per row. On every row the SAVE and LOAD VMM offsets are equal and the hook logs no error. ¹ Batched Qwen3.5 differs by 0.002 on every pair, native/save included (DeltaNet batch composition), so not from the restore. The gpt-oss output is not comparable (dummy mxfp4 experts); graph == load parity holds and save/load sequential is exact. Its LOAD TPOT is 5-9% above native (two samples) because its MoE swiglu (`swiglu_gpt_oss_sigmoid_alpha`) is a real `torch.compile` fusion that runs as eager kernels under the Dynamo pin; a native engine launched with the same pin runs at `load` speed (bs 1/8/32/128: native 5.08 / 5.29 / 6.05 / 9.26 ms, native with the pin 5.56 / 5.77 / 6.54 / 9.72, `load` 5.50 / 5.71 / 6.46 / 9.61). With `--moe-runner-backend triton_kernel` (TP4, ep_size 1), whose activation is a hand-written kernel, `load` equals native (3.57 / 3.81 / 4.27 / 5.99 vs 3.58 / 3.76 / 4.24 / 5.97 ms) and the strict check is exact on every pair. On the attention-TP rows `load` TPOT reads 5-8% below native. That is not the graphs: a profiler window at bs 32 shows identical kernel counts and per-step kernel time on both engines. The native engines in these runs did not have `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1`, so their eager steps (bs below the TP multiple, mixed steps) pay Dynamo's guard checks and graph-break frames per MoE layer; a native engine launched with the same pin matches `load` (Qwen3-30B attn TP2 x DP2 + EP4, bs 1/8/32/128: native 100.3 / 13.9 / 21.4 / 23.5 ms, native with the pin 93.7 / 13.0 / 20.1 / 23.5, `load` 92.2 / 12.8 / 20.0 / 22.1). The EP-only rows run every batch as a graph and show no gap. One SGLang-side observation from the runs, not caused by this PR: with attention TP > 1, a FULL prefill bucket that is not divisible by the TP size cannot be captured. The layer boundary reduce-scatters tokens over attention TP; real batches are padded, but the capture bucket is not. +---
+title: "CUDA Graph Persistence"
+metatags:
+    description: "Save the captured CUDA graphs once and restore them on later starts with Foundry (--cuda-graph-persistence)."
+---
+
+## Overview
+
+CUDA graph capture (kernel warmup, attention-metadata setup and one capture per batch size) is a large part of a server's cold start. With `--cuda-graph-persistence`, [Foundry](https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry) saves the captured graphs, together with the memory layout they reference, on a first start (`save`) and rebuilds them from that archive on later starts (`load`) instead of capturing.
+
+Foundry runs a CUDA driver hook in the scheduler processes that places every device allocation at the same address on `save` and `load`.
+
+## Installation
+
+Foundry is an optional dependency, published on PyPI as `foundry-core` (import name `foundry`):
+
+```bash
+pip install "sglang[foundry]"
+```
+
+The PyPI wheel is built against the torch SGLang pins. For another torch / CUDA pair, add the pair's package index (`whl/<cuda>/torch<A.B>/`, see the [Foundry README](https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry#installation)):
+
+```bash
+pip install "sglang[foundry]" --extra-index-url https://foundry-org.github.io/foundry/whl/cu130/torch2.13/
+```
+
+## Usage
+
+```bash
+# First start: capture as usual and write the archive (./foundry_archive by default).
+sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --cuda-graph-persistence save
+
+# Later starts: restore the graphs from the archive.
+sglang serve --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-1.7B --cuda-graph-persistence load
+```
+
+**Engines with `--cuda-graph-persistence` run with `TORCHDYNAMO_DISABLE=1`.** Foundry pins it for the scheduler processes and rejects a contrary value: with TorchDynamo on, `save` fails at the first `@torch.compile` helper inside the capture window on torch 2.14 and later. The validated models show no difference in output or TPOT.
+
+`--cuda-graph-persistence-config` names an optional Foundry TOML (`workspace_root` for the archive directory, `base_addr` / `region_size` for the address region, `scratch_space_size`); its `mode` key is ignored, the flag's mode wins:
+
+```toml
+workspace_root = "/data/foundry_archive/qwen3-1.7b"
+region_size = "256GB"
+```
+
+`save` and `load` must use the same model, flags, parallel layout and GPU type; remove the archive before a `save` of another configuration.
+
+The launcher and every scheduler log one activation line, and `load` logs the restore per runner:
+
+```text
+[Foundry] cuda graph persistence active: pid=<pid> mode=load config=<toml or None>
+[Foundry] Loaded <N> SGLang graphs in <s>s
+```
+
+Run engines with and without `--cuda-graph-persistence` in separate processes.
+
+## What it changes
+
+- Decode graphs use the `full` backend; prefill graphs are `full` or `disabled` (default `disabled`). Other backends are rejected.
+- Flags and environment variables that select state a restored graph cannot replay (custom all-reduce IPC buffers, NCCL symmetric memory / NVLS / buffer registration, MSCCL++, two-batch overlap, the memory saver, graph-pool borrow / precarve, the metadata glue graph) are pinned; each pin prints a `[Foundry] pin:` line, and an explicit contrary value stops the launch with the reason.
+- Speculative decoding is supported for EAGLE / EAGLE3 (target-verify, draft-decode and draft-extend graphs; not adaptive or multi-layer EAGLE); other speculative algorithms, LoRA, PD multiplexing, elastic-EP graph recapture and post-capture KV sizing are not supported.

+"""Adapter for Foundry CUDA graph persistence (``--cuda-graph-persistence``).
+
+Foundry (https://github.com/foundry-org/foundry, PyPI ``foundry-core``,
+optional dependency ``sglang[foundry]``) saves the captured CUDA graphs and
+the memory layout they reference on a first start (``save``) and rebuilds
+them from that archive on later starts (``load``) instead of capturing. It runs a CUDA driver hook in
+the scheduler processes (``LD_PRELOAD``, set by ``configure_subprocess()``
+around their spawn) and is called from the call sites below; the methods of
+the no-op adapter do nothing, so the call sites stay unconditional.
+
+Call sites: the resolution steps in ``arg_groups/cuda_graph_hook.py``,
+``_set_envs_and_config`` and the scheduler spawns (``entrypoints/engine.py``,
+``managers/data_parallel_controller.py``), ``run_scheduler_process``,
+``bootstrap.init_parallel_runtime``, ``ModelRunner.init_torch_distributed`` and
+``alloc_memory_pool``, ``KVCacheConfigurator._resolve_memory_pool_config``, the
+decode / prefill runners' ``capture``, and
+``FullCudaGraphBackend.capture_one``. Every call passes the values Foundry
+needs (the loaded model, the draft-worker flag, the resolved pool config, the
+prefill request slots, the decode-type runner's graph kind); no runner or
+backend object crosses the boundary. The decode runner's ``capture`` is also
+reached by its speculative-decoding subclasses (the EAGLE draft and
+draft-extend runners) and by the target-verify runner; each passes its
+``kind`` (``target_decode``, ``target_verify``, ``draft_decode``,
+``draft_extend``) so Foundry archives and restores the graph sets apart.
+Restored decode graphs carry no in-graph shared-read marker; the decode
+runner's own fallback for that case (POST_REPLAY) is the fence they need.
+
+Foundry is imported only when the flag is set: importing it loads its CUDA
+extension, which a server without the flag must not pay for.
+
+Process contract: a process is persistence-enabled from its first
+``activate_foundry`` or never. Activation preloads Foundry's CUDA driver hook
+into the children, reserves the allocation region and pins environment
+variables, none of which can be undone in a live process (resetting the
+adapter would not clear them), so a later record without
+``--cuda-graph-persistence`` in an enabled process is an error, not a
+fallback to the no-op adapter.
+"""
+
+import logging
+from contextlib import contextmanager
+from typing import Any, Optional
+
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+
+# Version of foundry.integration.sglang.api this adapter calls: same major,
+# at least this minor.
+FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MAJOR = 2
+FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MIN_MINOR = 1
+# Distribution name (import name ``foundry``) and minimum version, checked
+# when the flag is set.
+FOUNDRY_PACKAGE = "foundry-core"
+FOUNDRY_MIN_VERSION = "0.1.0rc2"
+FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT = (
+    'Install it with `pip install "sglang[foundry]"` (package foundry-core; see '
+    "docs/advanced_features/cuda_graph_persistence)."
+)
+
+
+class FoundryAdapter:
+    """No-op base: what every process uses unless ``--cuda-graph-persistence``
+    is set."""
+
+    enabled = False
+    mode: Optional[str] = None
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def create(
+        enable: bool, mode: Optional[str] = None, config_path: Optional[str] = None
+    ) -> "FoundryAdapter":
+        if not enable:
+            return FoundryAdapter()
+        return _FoundryAdapterReal(_import_foundry_api(), mode, config_path)
+
+    # Resolution (launcher).
+    def pin_server_args(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def validate_graph_config(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def validate_resolved_server_args(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def apply_env_pins(self, server_args: Any) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    # Process spawn.
+    @contextmanager
+    def configure_subprocess(self, server_args: Any = None):
+        yield
+
+    # Scheduler process.
+    def before_parallel_init(self, device: str) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def after_parallel_init(self) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def after_runner_distributed_init(self, is_draft_worker: bool) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def replay_saved_memory_pool_config(self):
+        return None
+
+    def record_memory_pool_overrides(self) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def before_alloc_memory_pool(self, is_draft_worker: bool) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    def after_alloc_memory_pool(
+        self, memory_pool_config: Any, is_draft_worker: bool
+    ) -> None:
+        pass
+
+    @contextmanager
+    def capture_scope(
+        self,
+        phase: str,
+        *,
+        model: Any,
+        req_slots: Optional[int] = None,
+        kind: Optional[str] = None,
+    ):
+        """``phase`` is "decode" (with the runner's graph ``kind``) or
+        "prefill" (with the runner's fixed request slots); ``model`` is the
+        runner's loaded model."""
+        yield
+
+    def capture_one(
+        self,
+        shape_key: Any,
+        forward_fn,
+        *,
+        pool: Any,
+        stream: Any,
+    ):
+        """Returns ``(graph, output)`` for the backend to store."""
+        raise RuntimeError("capture_one is only called when Foundry is enabled")
+
+
+class _FoundryAdapterReal(FoundryAdapter):
+    enabled = True
+
+    def __init__(self, api, mode: str, config_path: Optional[str]):
+        self._api = api
+        self.mode = mode
+        api.activate(mode=mode, config_path=config_path)
+
+    def pin_server_args(self, server_args):
+        self._api.pin_server_args(server_args)
+
+    def validate_graph_config(self, server_args):
+        self._api.validate_graph_config(server_args)
+
+    def validate_resolved_server_args(self, server_args):
+        self._api.validate_resolved_server_args(server_args)
+
+    def apply_env_pins(self, server_args):
+        self._api.apply_env_pins(server_args)
+
+    def configure_subprocess(self, server_args=None):
+        return self._api.configure_subprocess(server_args)
+
+    def before_parallel_init(self, device):
+        self._api.before_parallel_init(device)
+
+    def after_parallel_init(self):
+        self._api.after_parallel_init()
+
+    def after_runner_distributed_init(self, is_draft_worker):
+        self._api.after_runner_distributed_init(is_draft_worker)
+
+    def replay_saved_memory_pool_config(self):
+        return self._api.replay_saved_memory_pool_config()
+
+    def record_memory_pool_overrides(self):
+        self._api.record_memory_pool_overrides()
+
+    def before_alloc_memory_pool(self, is_draft_worker):
+        self._api.before_alloc_memory_pool(is_draft_worker)
+
+    def after_alloc_memory_pool(self, memory_pool_config, is_draft_worker):
+        self._api.after_alloc_memory_pool(memory_pool_config, is_draft_worker)
+
+    def capture_scope(self, phase, *, model, req_slots=None, kind=None):
+        return self._api.capture_scope(
+            phase, model=model, req_slots=req_slots, kind=kind
+        )
+
+    def capture_one(self, shape_key, forward_fn, *, pool, stream):
+        return self._api.capture_one(shape_key, forward_fn, pool=pool, stream=stream)
+
+
+def _import_foundry_api():
+    try:
+        from foundry.integration.sglang import api
+    except ImportError as e:
+        logger.warning(
+            "--cuda-graph-persistence is set, but Foundry is not installed. %s",
+            FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT,
+        )
+        raise e
+    from sglang.srt.utils.common import assert_pkg_version
+
+    assert_pkg_version(FOUNDRY_PACKAGE, FOUNDRY_MIN_VERSION, FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT)
+    found = getattr(api, "INTEGRATION_API_VERSION", None)
+    if (
+        found is None
+        or found[0] != FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MAJOR
+        or found[1] < FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MIN_MINOR
+    ):
+        raise RuntimeError(
+            f"Foundry integration API {found} is not supported by this SGLang, which "
+            f"needs {FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MAJOR}.x with x >= "
+            f"{FOUNDRY_INTEGRATION_API_MIN_MINOR}. {FOUNDRY_INSTALL_HINT}"
+        )
+    return api
+
+
+_NOOP = FoundryAdapter()
+_active: FoundryAdapter = _NOOP
+
+
+def get_foundry_adapter() -> FoundryAdapter:
+    """This process's adapter: the one ``activate_foundry`` created, else the
+    no-op one."""
+    return _active
+
+
+def activate_foundry(server_args: Any) -> FoundryAdapter:
+    """This process's adapter for ``server_args``, from its raw
+    ``--cuda-graph-persistence`` and ``--cuda-graph-persistence-config``.
+
+    Without the flag: the no-op adapter, and an error if this process already
+    activated Foundry (see the process contract in the module docstring).
+    With it: activates Foundry on the first call; later calls must name the
+    same mode and config. Run by the first resolution step in the launcher and
+    at the top of the scheduler and data-parallel-controller processes."""
+    global _active
+    mode = server_args.cuda_graph_persistence
+    if mode is None:
+        if _active.enabled:
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                "Foundry CUDA graph persistence is active in this process "
+                f"(--cuda-graph-persistence {_active.mode}), and a server_args "
+                "without it cannot run here: Foundry's CUDA hook, allocation region "
+                "and environment pins cannot be undone in a live process. Use a "
+                "separate process for engines without --cuda-graph-persistence."
+            )
+        return _NOOP
+    config_path = server_args.cuda_graph_persistence_config
+    if _active.enabled:
+        # A second record in the same process must name the same archive.
+        _active._api.activate(mode=mode, config_path=config_path)
+        return _active
+    _active = FoundryAdapter.create(True, mode=mode, config_path=config_path)
+    return _active

+# The requirement of the sglang[foundry] extra, read from pyproject.toml so the pin lives in one place.
+FOUNDRY_SPEC=$(grep -Po -m1 '"\Kfoundry-core[^"]*' python/pyproject.toml)

+FOUNDRY_INDEX=$(python3 - <<'PY'

+)

+    # the KV pool included; 256GB covers an 80-192 GB GPU at this memory fraction.

+            f'workspace_root = "{workspace}"\nscratch_space_size = "1024MB"\n'

+    metrics = requests.get(base_url + "/metrics", timeout=30).text
